transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Life from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says he'll fight any effort in Congress
to impeach him over the war in Iran.
In a video posted on Thursday, Hegseth defended his handling of the conflict
and took aim at his critics on Capitol Hill.
>> You see, their policies don't work, so their obsession with political theater
disguised as power drives them to try to destroy their opponents.
It's all about the politics of personal destruction.
Didn't work against President Trump, and it won't work with me.
>> Kentucky Republican Tom Massey says he plans to force a House vote
to impeach Hegseth when lawmakers return next week.
Critics accused him of continuing the war without congressional authorization.
President Trump has publicly supported Hegseth.
A federal judge has blocked construction on President Trump's proposed arch
for two weeks, and PR's Rachel Treisman reports a federal planning commission
had given final approval for the project, clearing the way for the work to begin.
>> Over 130 people signed up to speak at the National Capitol Planning Commission meeting,
overwhelmingly against the arch.
The Trump-friendly panel gave it the green light,
despite the public pushback and an ongoing legal challenge.
District Judge Tonya Chetkin issued a late-night order blocking construction for 14 days.
In her opinion, she seems skeptical of the government's conflicting motivations
for building the arch, and it's argument that congressional approval is not needed.
Democratic lawmakers have said they will use their new congressional majority
to not only block the arch, but investigate possible wrongdoing.
Rachel Treisman, NPR News.
>> One of the major takeaways from the 2024 election was that Democrats lost ground
with young voters who shifted right toward Donald Trump.
But this week, voters under the age of 30 issued a strong rebuke of the president
and his party, voting decisively for Democrats.
NPR's Alina Moore reports.
>> In recent elections, Democrats have done well when they win young voters
by a margin of at least 20 points.
On Tuesday, they carried the group by nearly 50 points, according to exit polls.
It's the largest margin Democrats have had with young people in decades.
And though young voters do turn out at lower rates than older voters,
that sizable support made a difference on the margins.
An example, the Texas Senate race.
Democrat James Tallarico won the state by 12 percentage points.
Looking at just Gen Z, though, voters under 30, he won it by 60 points.
Alina Moore, NPR News, Washington.
>> The Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska are still too close to call.
In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Cologne leads Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith
by fewer than 2,000 votes.
In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican Senator Dan Sullivan
by about 600 votes.
This is NPR News.
The French government is trying to quell a protest movement now into its second month.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports the prime minister will meet with union heads
and businesses on Monday to come up with possible solutions.
>> Upbeat protests across France Thursday drew record crowds.
What began as a student movement for better learning conditions
has widened into large-scale anger over low salaries,
skyrocketing prices and inequalities.
Dominique Muizi, head of a public policy think tank, the Multania Institute,
says addressing inequality is key to ending the protest.
>> Something has to move in order to restore some kind of equality amongst Frenchmen
because the explosion of inequality is really behind what we have been witnessing
since the beginning of these demonstrations.
>> More nationwide protests are planned over the weekend.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
Authorities in Europe are reporting more bomb threats against commercial flights today,
a string of hoaxes for some planes to divert earlier this week.
The French prime minister's office says four new threats targeted aircraft over France.
In Hungary, the defense minister says fighter jets escorted three passenger planes
through the country's airspace.
Two broadcasters also received threats prompting newsrooms to evacuate their offices.
No suspicious items were found.
Stocks are trading higher at the sour on Wall Street.
The Dow is up 23 points.
The NASDAQ composite up 398.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.

Judge Tonya Chutkan blocks construction of Trump's arch for two weeks
Young voters under 30 broke decisively for Democrats in this week's elections
Mississippi and Alaska Senate races too close to call; Hyde-Smith and Sullivan trail
French protests grow into record crowds; prime minister to meet unions and businesses Monday
European authorities report more bomb hoaxes against commercial flights; no suspicious items found
Stocks trade higher on Wall Street, with the Dow up 23 points and Nasdaq up 398
